items.heading: Turmeric / Haldi
details: Contains curcuminoids with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory biological activity.

items.heading: Neem
details: Contains compounds with insecticidal and insect-repellent properties.

items.heading: Tulsi
details: Contains several biologically active phytochemicals used across many traditional remedies.

items.heading: Ginger / Adrak
details: Contains bioactive compounds, with some evidence supporting traditional nausea-related uses.

items.heading: Garlic / Lahsun
details: Contains biologically active sulfur compounds studied for a range of health effects.

items.heading: Amla
details: A nutrient-rich fruit containing vitamin C and a range of protective phytochemicals.

items.heading: Fenugreek / Methi
details: Contains dietary fiber and bioactive compounds used in traditional cooking and remedies.

items.heading: Cumin / Jeera
details: Contains aromatic volatile compounds and phytochemicals used widely in Indian cooking.

items.heading: Black pepper / Kali Mirch
details: Piperine, its key compound, can increase the body's absorption of some other compounds.

items.heading: Cinnamon / Dalchini
details: Contains bioactive plant compounds studied for various metabolic effects.

items.heading: Cardamom / Elaichi
details: Contains aromatic phytochemicals valued both in cooking and traditional remedies.

items.heading: Clove / Laung
details: Its eugenol content has antimicrobial and local analgesic (pain-relieving) properties.

items.heading: Ajwain
details: Contains thymol and other volatile compounds traditionally associated with digestive relief.

items.heading: Asafoetida / Hing
details: Contains volatile compounds traditionally associated with digestive preparations.
